GoingPlaces: Defines the profit motive and dramatizes the part it has played in the economic development of our country. Stresses the need for continued industrial profits if our economic vitality is to endure.

rv: Very smooth and entertaining look at the urban sprawl problem. And, in an interesting comparison to 'Give Yourself The Green Light', this film advoacates more public transit as being the more feasible option (which is so true). Quite an entertaining beginning, with how traffic all got started, and where we are today. The film suggests more busses, cable cars and subways as viable options of moving people around. This film is FILLED with great camera angles (watch how a cable car turns and misses the camera by THIS much). The only unfortunate problem with this is, it's spliced to hell. :( But…

The film simply states that mass transportation is one solution to pollution, congestion, wall to wall pavement and multitudes of jackasses on the road at the same time to work each morning. However.....that would put two major industries in profit jeopardy. Who would that be? hmmmmm? Research the demise of the So. Cal Redline rail for a concise model.

The shot list is for a John Sutherland cartoon with the same name. It has nothing to do with this film. There's a full-page ad for this short in the Aug. 1953 edition of "The American City" magazine. "More than 70 prints of “Going Places” are now in the hands of civic leaders and transit officials across the country." Marvin Miller narrates a familiar story of traffic clogs only being solved by mass transit. Same problem 70 years later, except you can add e-bikes and scooters to the mix.
